text:
Carla R: Starting the 22:00 change window now. Rolling service-api v2026.03.1 -> hosted region eu-west with standard canary (10% -> 50% -> 100%). Preflight SLO checks kicked off. I’ll post any smoke alerts here.

deploy-bot: Deploy initiated: service-api v2026.03.1
- canary: 10%
- rollout_plan: linear-30m
- runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/deploy-checks

Ben (oncall): Observability note: dashboards up at https://grafana.redwood/service-api?from=now-1h. P95 baseline ~120ms. I see a small p95 blip to ~210ms in one host pool already. :eyes:

Maya P: lmk if we should hold at 10%. I can pin traffic back to v2026.02.4 quickly if noise increases.

Jordan L: Uploading a quick metric snapshot. 5xx rate from canary is 0.18% -> 0.95% over last 4m, most are 502 upstream errors. Stack traces show kvcache misses flooding origin.

Jordan L: snippet:
```
[2026-03-20T22:03:12Z] svc:request failed status=502 upstream_timeout route=/complete
[2026-03-20T22:04:01Z] kvcache: miss rate 74% -> 91% under canary
```

Ben (oncall): Flags to consider: hold, partial rollback to v2026.02.4, or route canary to eu-west-dedicated (isolates traffic). Also consider reducing concurrency/batch size for canary pool (config: batch.max_tokens=512 -> 256).

Carla R: Setting a hold on the linear ramp for now. Holding at 10% while we triage. Can someone run the kvcache GC/metrics check on the canary nodes?

Maya P: I’ll trigger a quick config tweak: lowering batch size and enabling prefix cache warmup for canary nodes. Patch command:
```
kubectl -n hosted set env ds/service-api BATCH_MAX_TOKENS=256 PREFIX_CACHE_WARMUP=true --context=eu-west-canary
```

deploy-bot: Config rollout queued. 3 pods will restart sequentially.

Ben (oncall): After the env change p95 dropped to 145ms and 5xx back to 0.25% in the last 5m. Still elevated vs baseline but much improved. Suggest keep canary at 10% for another 20m, increase sampling for evals, and re-run canary load test. :thumbsup:

Maya P: Updated release notes draft (internal): "v2026.03.1: runtime kvcache instrumentation, attention kernel tweaks, adjusted batching defaults." Will push to public notes after final pass.

Jordan L: Re-running the canary synthetic for heavy prefix miss: https://loadtest.redwood/canary/2026-03-20. Initial run shows stable 200qps, latency p95 ~150-160ms. No regression in output quality detected on sampling.

Carla R: Decision: keep hold, increase canary to 20% at T+25m if no new 5xx or p95>200ms incidents. If 5xx >0.5% for 3 consecutive 5m windows, automatic rollback to v2026.02.4. Noted in runbook.

sre-bot: Change-window policy updated:
- canary_threshold: 0.5% 5xx
- p95_threshold: 200ms
- auto_rollback: enabled -> target_version v2026.02.4

Ben (oncall): I’ll keep monitoring dash and alerts. Will escalate if error budget burn spikes.

Maya P: I’ll also add a temporary logging level increase on the canary path to capture request ids for any new 502s.

Carla R: Thanks all. Please annotate the deploy ticket with these checks and tag @release for post-window notes. If all good, plan to finish ramp to 100% tomorrow morning during the next quiet window.

Jordan L: quick note: we saw a single client retry loop that amplified upstream timeouts. Filed a small fix PR to throttle retries on the client side, will include in the follow-up patch.

Ben (oncall): 22:35 update: canary at 10% -> metrics stable for 30m. p95 hovering 130-150ms, 5xx steady at 0.1%. Going to green-check and approve move to 20% at +25m. :white_check_mark:

Carla R: moving to 20% now. Rolling change recorded.

deploy-bot: Traffic adjusted: canary -> 20%

Maya P: Noted. I’ll sync release notes and include a small troubleshooting blurb about kvcache warmup.

Carla R: Closing thread for active triage. Will open a follow-up if anything regresses. Good ops on the quick patch and monitoring. :clap:
